answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks through remote hardware attestation. Agents must present cryptographic proofs signed by secure hardware enclaves to interact. An attacker incurs the verifiable hardware expense of procuring dedicated physical silicon per identity. Validated identities lock into a glacier epoch so unverified clones cannot wander into consensus. However, relying on an ivory root of trust ties protocol security to centralized chip vendors who can revoke signing keys.
